attributes.scope: MWCC GC 1.2.5 family; applies to any reconstruction that reads the same `extern f32/f64 lbl_*` pool pseudo-global at 2+ nearby sites, especially where the intervening stores go through f32*/u8*-derived pointers. Sibling of claim.law.extern-scalar-read-defeats-fp-literal-hoist, which governs the literal-vs-extern SPELLING choice; this law governs the number of READS of a correctly-spelled extern.

subject: compiler:mwcc-gc-1.2.5
value: Repeating a read of the same `extern f32/f64 lbl_*` pool global at N nearby sites compiles to N separate lfs/lfd loads, because a store through any f32*/u8*-derived pointer may alias the global and kills the CSE. The target frequently loads such a value ONCE and holds it in an FPR across the whole run of stores. The fix is a LOCAL initialised from the extern (`f32 z = lbl_80345EC8;`) used at every site: the local is not memory, so no store can invalidate it and MWCC keeps it in one register -- and when the uses sit in a loop, assigning the local just before the loop is what puts the load in target's pre-loop block instead of the loop body. Diagnostic tell: --ops shows ours-only lfs/lfd with NO target counterpart, and the aligned diff shows a repeated `lfs fX,0(0) @lbl_*(EMB_SDA21)` between otherwise matching stores. This is the exact inverse of claim.law.extern-zero-init-blocks-constant-propagation, and the two must not be confused: that law forbids replacing the extern READ with a C literal (which would let MWCC constant-propagate and delete stores the target kept); this law says keep the extern read, just perform it ONCE into a local. Both are satisfied simultaneously by `f32 z = lbl_*;` -- the initializer stays an opaque memory load while the uses become register reads. Caution measured in the same pass: over-applying it is possible -- collapsing six reads to one at a site where target kept two left our stream 2 lfs SHORT of target, so A/B each run rather than sweeping a whole function, and check the sign of the lfs delta in the multiset after every batch.
